evidence.excerpt:
Deep research agents decompose open-ended
queries into subtasks, retrieve web evidence
over multiple rounds, and synthesize long-form
reports. This workflow creates a planning-
layer poisoning surface: adversarial documents
that enter the retrieval pool can steer follow-up
questions and turn a local injection into report-
level contamination. We present FORGE
(FabricatedOrchestratedReasoning chain for
aGentExploitation), a two-level attack that
combines intra-document reasoning fabrication
with inter-document chain coordination to hi-
jack subtask planning. We further introduce
PRISMmetric, which weights infected report
claims by cognitive type, and Root Query An-
choring, a lightweight defense that ties recur-
sive follow-up generation to the root query.
Across 25 queries, Network FORGE reaches
26.4% PRISM with five injected documents
and exhibits depth migration, in which recur-
sive

evidence.excerpt:
FORGE addresses two failure points that single-
layer poisoning leaves exposed: a single document
looks like an unsupported assertion, and a flat set
of documents looks like coincidental overlap rather
than evidence. We therefore design the attack at
two levels: each adversarial document carries an
internal reasoning chain that makes its assigned
claim appear locally derived, and the full docu-
ment set is organized as a distributed argument
chain that makes the collection appear as conver-
gent multi-source evidence. Given a target narra-
tive V, FORGE constructs j adversarial documents
P={p 1, . . . , pj} that steer the final report R to-
ward that narrative. Sections 4.1 and 4.2 formalize
these two construction levels; Section 4.3 shows
how they escalate to report-level contamination
through subtask hijacking.

and research depth, all sharing the same PRISM
pipeline for cross-setting comparison.
Platform and models.We use gpt-
researcher (Elovic, 2023) as the testbed, with
gpt-4o-mini (OpenAI, 2024a) for search and
filtering, gpt-4.1 (OpenAI, 2025b) for sub-
reports and final synthesis, and o4-mini (OpenAI,
2025c) for planning. Claim extraction, type
classification, and infection detection (§ 5) use
Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite(DeepMind, 2026).

m+j pool via Eq. (1) with α= 0.4
andtext-embedding-3-small (OpenAI, 2024b).
Only the top m reach synthesis, so adversarial doc-
uments mustdisplacegenuine ones rather than ex-
pand the evidence set.

A controlled transplant separates the two chan-

the subtask lists from normal FORGE runs atj= 1
and j= 5 (nc ∈ {1,5}) with retrieval injection at
j∈ {1,5}, holding the plan fixed while varying
only evidence volume (Fig. 4). The asymmetry
is stark. Under the fixed j= 1 plan, scaling re-
trieval fivefold leaves PRISM unchanged (14.1%
→ 14.1%); the extra poisoned documents are effec-
tively inert. Swapping in thej= 5 plan, even at the
lowest retrieval setting, lifts PRISM to 22.8%, and
combining both channels reaches 29.5%. A weakly
poisoned subtask list thus limits the effect of in-
jected evidence, since its retrieval queries rarely
target V-aligned

This subsection validates the claim-typing accuracy
of the PRISM evaluator (§ 5). Two human anno-
tators, neither of whom is an author of this paper,
independently assigned a claim type to each of 206
claims drawn from the depth experiment; disagree-
ments were adjudicated by a third annotator, and
cases where the final label differed from the model
prediction were recorded as corrections. Table 5
summarizes the agreement rates by claim type.
Overall agreement is 92.7%, with Cohen's κ=
0.905. Most disagreements occur at the bound-
ary between causal, factual, and evaluative claims.
Representative causal-label disagreements include:
•"Strong IP protections are essential for recoup-
ing high R&D costs in patent-driven fields. "
The model labels the claim as causal, while
the human label is evaluative.
•"Regulatory pressure is the primary driver for
the adoption of closed-loop cooling

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding attack efficacy, the role of subtask hijacking as the central bottleneck, depth migration from framing to factual contamination, and RQA mitigation are backed directly by quantitative tables, ablations, and qualitative excerpts.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is thorough, assessing local and network poisoning across 25 queries in 5 categories, depth levels, baseline models (PoisonedRAG, AuthChain), and structural component ablations. Causal isolation using a subtask transplant design cleanly proves that subtask hijacking rather than raw retrieval volume drives contamination, and RQA is benchmarked against standard defenses showing reduced PRISM and improved report utility.
primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss key limitations including testbed architecture dependency, lack of live-web authority/spam filtering dynamics in retrieval simulation, heuristic weight assignment in PRISM, and susceptibility of RQA to adaptive retrieval-focused adversaries.
primary.method_assessment: The threat model and attack mechanism are thoroughly formalized, showing how adversarial documents steer subtask generation to compound poisoned retrieval across multi-round workflows. The PRISM metric explicitly addresses limitations of binary attack success rates in long-form generation, and its evaluation pipeline is accompanied by rigorous human validation studies reporting high agreement and Cohen's kappa.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents an original, methodologically sound, and extensively validated investigation of adversarial vulnerabilities specific to recursive LLM research agents, adhering to rigorous empirical standards.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper identifies the planning-layer vulnerability in recursive deep research agents, introduces FORGE (an attack coupling intra-document reasoning fabrication with inter-document chaining), formulates PRISM (a cognitive-type weighted severity metric for report poisoning), and proposes Root Query Anchoring (RQA) as a planning-layer defense.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents an original, methodologically sound, and extensively validated investigation of adversarial vulnerabilities specific to recursive LLM research agents, adhering to rigorous empirical standards.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly discuss key limitations including testbed architecture dependency, lack of live-web authority/spam filtering dynamics in retrieval simulation, heuristic weight assignment in PRISM, and susceptibility of RQA to adaptive retrieval-focused adversaries.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
